hero.title: Meet your personal AI agent
hero.lead: A personal AI agent is one assistant that lives on your own computer and does real work for you — reading, researching, planning, remembering, acting. Each card below is a complete setup guide for one thing it can do. Follow any one of them, and the rest are just a message away.

features.title: Private by design
features.desc: Lives on your computer, not someone else's cloud.

features.title: Chat from anywhere
features.desc: Telegram, WhatsApp, or the phone app.

features.title: Pay per use
features.desc: A few dollars a month. No subscription.

features.title: No skills needed
features.desc: Each card is a complete recipe, start to finish.

install.title: Install Wolffish on your computer
install.body: Download it free at wolffi.sh for macOS, Windows, or Linux — or, if you like terminals, run one line:
install.note: Open Wolffish when it finishes. It asks for your language and theme, then offers to set up local models — choose “Skip for now”; you'll connect a smarter cloud brain in the next step.

key.title: Give it a brain — a DeepSeek key
key.body: Wolffish is the agent; DeepSeek is the intelligence it runs on — excellent and famously cheap. Create a key at platform.deepseek.com: sign up, add a few dollars of credit, open “API Keys”, create one, and copy it. Back in Wolffish, open Settings → Models → DeepSeek, paste the key, and click Save. Finally, click the model picker beside the message box and choose “DeepSeek V4 Pro”.
key.note: Pay-as-you-go, no subscription — typical daily use costs a few dollars a month, and Settings → Usage shows exactly what you spend.

keyVision.title: Give it a brain that can see — a Grok key
keyVision.body: This use case involves photos, so Wolffish needs a model with vision. Create a key at console.x.ai: sign up, open “API Keys”, create one, and copy it. Back in Wolffish, open Settings → Models → xAI, paste the key, and click Save. Finally, click the model picker beside the message box and choose “Grok 4.6”.
keyVision.note: Grok 4.6 handles text and images. It costs more than text-only models, but for personal use it's still just a few dollars a month — Settings → Usage keeps count.

brave.title: Add sharper web search — free
brave.body: Wolffish can already search the web, but a free Brave key makes results faster and cleaner. Create one at brave.com/search/api, then in Wolffish open Settings → Services → Brave Search, switch it on, paste the key, and click Save.
brave.note: Optional — skip it and Wolffish quietly uses DuckDuckGo instead. Brave's free tier is plenty for personal use.

workspace.title: Connect your Google account
workspace.body: This gives Wolffish real access to your Gmail and Calendar — through Google's own sign-in, with everything stored only on your computer. In Wolffish, open Settings → Services → Google Workspace and follow the panel top to bottom: click Install (a small Google helper tool), then follow the built-in “Create an OAuth Client” guide — it walks you through Google's console click by click and ends with downloading a small file. Drop that file into the panel, click Authorize, and approve in your browser.
workspace.note: Honest warning: this is the fiddliest step on this whole page — about ten minutes of clicking through Google's console, one time only. The in-app guide holds your hand the entire way.

telegram.title: Create your private Telegram bot
telegram.body: In Telegram, message @BotFather, send /newbot, and follow its two prompts — it hands you a token. Then message @userinfobot to get your personal ID number. Back in Wolffish, open Settings → Channels → Telegram, switch it on, paste the token, put your ID in “Allowed user IDs”, and click Save. Now open your new bot in Telegram and say hi.
telegram.note: The bot is completely private: it only ever answers the IDs you allow, and the token never leaves your machine.

whatsapp.title: Link WhatsApp
whatsapp.body: In Wolffish, open Settings → Channels → WhatsApp, switch it on, and click Connect — a QR code appears. On your phone, open WhatsApp → Settings → Linked Devices → Link a Device and scan it. Then type your own phone number into “Allowed phone numbers”. To chat with Wolffish, open WhatsApp and message yourself — search your own name and use the “Message yourself” chat.
whatsapp.note: Only numbers on the allowed list get answered; everyone else is ignored. The link survives restarts — you won't scan again unless you unlink it.

mobile.title: Put Wolffish in your pocket
mobile.body: Install the free Wolffish app on your phone, then pair it: on your computer open Settings → Channels → Mobile and generate a Pairing QR; on your phone tap “Connect to Desktop” and scan it. From then on you can chat, watch tasks run, approve actions, and get notifications from anywhere.
mobile.note: Phone and computer talk through an end-to-end encrypted tunnel — no account, no password, and no copy of your chats in any cloud.

morning-briefing.title: Your morning briefing
morning-briefing.desc: Wake up to one message: today's calendar, the emails that matter, the weather, and news on your topics.
morning-briefing.intro: By the end of this guide, a personal briefing lands in your Telegram every morning — written for you, about your day — before you've opened a single app.

steps.title: Tell it what your mornings need
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send this — edit the time, city, and topics first:
prompt: Every day at 7:00 am, send me a morning briefing: my calendar for today, any important unread emails from the last 24 hours, today's weather in <your city>, and the top 3 stories about <topics you care about>. Keep it short and friendly.
steps.note: Wolffish saves this as an automation and confirms the schedule back to you. You can see or edit it any time on the Automations page in the app.

steps.title: Tune it like you'd tell a person
steps.body: After the first briefing arrives, just reply with adjustments — no settings screens:
prompt: Make the briefing shorter — bullet points only, skip the weather on weekends, and add a reminder of anyone whose birthday is this week.

morning-briefing.outro: Done. Tomorrow at 7:00 your day arrives in one message — and because Wolffish remembers, every “actually, also include…” makes it permanently better.

email.title: An assistant for your inbox
email.desc: Stop drowning in email. Wolffish reads, sorts, summarizes, and drafts replies — you just say the word.
email.intro: By the end of this guide, you can deal with a full inbox from a chat: “what needs me today?”, “draft a reply”, “find that invoice from March” — without opening Gmail.

steps.title: Try it on today's inbox
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send:
prompt: Summarize my unread emails from the last 24 hours. Group them into: needs a reply, good to know, and safe to ignore.

steps.title: Let it draft — you hit send
prompt: Draft a polite reply to the email from <name> saying I'm interested but need until Thursday to decide. Save it as a Gmail draft — don't send it.
steps.note: Drafts land in your Gmail drafts folder for you to review. Wolffish never sends mail unless you explicitly tell it to.

steps.title: Make it a daily habit
prompt: Every weekday at 5 pm, send me a summary of today's important emails and remind me which ones are still waiting on a reply from me.

email.outro: That's inbox peace: a morning “what needs me?”, drafts written while you have coffee, and a 5 pm sweep so nothing slips.

calendar.title: A calendar you can text
calendar.desc: “What's my week look like?” “Move Thursday's call to 4.” Manage your calendar by messaging it.
calendar.intro: By the end of this guide, your Google Calendar has a phone number: message it in WhatsApp to check, add, and move events in plain language.

steps.title: Ask about your week
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, send:
prompt: What's on my calendar this week? Anything double-booked?

steps.title: Add and move things in plain words
prompt: Schedule coffee with Sara on Thursday at 4 pm for an hour at <place>, and remind me the evening before.
Move my Thursday dentist appointment to Friday morning and let me know what's free.

steps.title: Get your week ahead, every Sunday
prompt: Every Sunday at 8 pm, send me my full week ahead with any gaps or conflicts pointed out.

calendar.outro: No more app-switching to answer “when are we free?” — your calendar now lives in the same place you already talk to people.

reminders.title: Reminders that find you
reminders.desc: Say it once, in your own words — get reminded on WhatsApp at exactly the right moment.
reminders.intro: By the end of this guide, anything you'd scribble on your hand goes to Wolffish instead — one-off errands, monthly bills, yearly renewals — and comes back to you at the right time.

steps.title: Set your first reminders
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, send a few — any phrasing works:
prompt: Remind me to renew my car registration on September 3rd at 9 am.
Remind me every first of the month to pay rent, and every Sunday evening to prep for the week.

steps.title: Too lazy to type? Talk
steps.body: Send a voice note instead — Wolffish transcribes it on your own computer, free, and sets the reminder just the same.
steps.note: Each reminder becomes an automation you can see and edit on the Automations page in the app — or just tell Wolffish “cancel the rent reminder”.

reminders.outro: Your head is no longer the storage system. With the phone app paired, reminders also arrive as push notifications — impossible to miss.

news.title: News, curated by you
news.desc: A twice-daily digest on exactly your topics — no feeds, no ads, no doomscrolling.
news.intro: By the end of this guide, the news comes to you: short, sourced, on your topics only, at the times you choose — and it learns what you skip.

steps.title: Order your digest
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send this — swap in your topics:
prompt: Every day at 8 am and 6 pm, search the web for the latest on <topic 1>, <topic 2>, and <topic 3>. Send the 5 most important stories as one-line bullets with links. Don't repeat stories you've already sent me.

steps.title: Steer it as you read
prompt: More depth on <topic 1>, drop <topic 3>, and add anything major about <your city>.

news.outro: You now have an editor working for you alone: two tight briefings a day, zero scrolling, and coverage that reshapes itself every time you give feedback.

social.title: Your social media scanner
social.desc: Wolffish watches the public web — X, Reddit, forums — for your name, brand, or topics, and reports back.
social.intro: By the end of this guide, you'll know what's being said — about you, your business, or the topics you track — without ever opening the apps. Wolffish searches public posts and summarizes what changed.

steps.title: Set the watch
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send this — with your own names and topics:
prompt: Every morning at 9, search the web — including public X and Reddit posts — for new mentions of <your name / brand / product> and new discussion about <a topic you track>. Summarize the mood, quote anything notable, and link the top posts. If nothing new, say so in one line.
steps.note: This works on public posts via web search — no social media logins or accounts required.

steps.title: Zoom in when something happens
prompt: Something's up in today's report — dig deeper into what people are saying about <the thing> and give me the full picture with links.

social.outro: You've replaced anxious scrolling with one calm daily report — and when something actually needs your attention, you'll hear about it first.

research.title: A researcher on call
research.desc: Hard questions, sourced answers: which laptop, which school, which insurance — compared properly.
research.intro: By the end of this guide, any decision that needs an hour of tabs — buying, choosing, comparing — becomes one message, answered with sources you can check.

steps.title: Give it a real decision
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, try one of these shapes:
prompt: Research the best <thing you're choosing> for <your situation> with a budget around <amount>. Compare the top 3 options in a table — price, pros, cons, what reviewers say — and end with your recommendation and source links.

steps.title: Get it as a shareable PDF
prompt: Turn that comparison into a clean one-page PDF I can send to my <partner / boss / friend>.

research.outro: That's an on-call researcher for the price of coffee — and with the phone app paired, you can hand it the next big question from anywhere and read the answer when it's done.

pdf.title: Talk to your PDFs
pdf.desc: Contracts, reports, manuals: send the file, ask questions, get summaries — even fill the forms.
pdf.intro: By the end of this guide, no PDF intimidates you: attach it in a chat and get plain-language answers, key numbers, deadlines, and red flags.

steps.title: Send a PDF, ask away
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, attach any PDF (tap the paperclip) and add:
prompt: Read this and give me: a plain-language summary, every date, deadline, and amount I should know about, and anything unusual I should be careful with.
steps.note: Telegram caps file downloads at 20 MB — for bigger files, drop them straight into the chat window of the desktop app.

steps.title: Let it do PDF chores
prompt: Merge the three PDFs I just sent into one file, in that order, and send it back.
Fill this form with my details — name <…>, date of birth <…>, address <…> — and send me the finished PDF.

pdf.outro: Summaries, answers, merges, filled forms — the paperwork skills you never wanted to learn, on call in your chat.

receipts.title: Receipts in, spreadsheet out
receipts.desc: Photograph receipts as you go. Wolffish reads them and keeps a tidy monthly expense sheet.
receipts.intro: By the end of this guide, expense tracking is one photo: snap the receipt, send it, forget it. Wolffish reads the details, keeps the running spreadsheet, and reports monthly.

steps.title: Teach it the routine
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, send:
prompt: From now on, whenever I send you a photo of a receipt, read it and add a row to my expense spreadsheet with: date, store, category, and amount. Confirm each one back to me in a single line.

steps.title: Snap your first receipt
steps.body: Photograph any receipt and send it. You'll get back something like “Added: Aug 18 — Grocery Mart — groceries — $42.10”. That's the whole workflow.
steps.note: Blurry photo? It will say what it couldn't read instead of guessing.

steps.title: Get the monthly picture
prompt: Every 1st of the month at 9 am, send me last month's expense spreadsheet plus a short breakdown by category and how it compares to the month before.

receipts.outro: A shoebox of receipts just became a clean spreadsheet that maintains itself — and every month you'll actually know where the money went.

memes.title: The group chat's meme machine
memes.desc: Describe the moment, get the meme — classic templates, custom captions, zero design skills.
memes.intro: By the end of this guide, you're the fastest meme in any group chat: describe the situation, get a finished image back, forward it while it's still relevant.

steps.title: Make your first meme
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send:
prompt: Make me a Drake meme — top: replying to every email myself; bottom: having my AI agent draft them.
steps.note: Works out of the box, no extra accounts. Want fancier templates or GIF search? Add free Giphy or Imgflip keys later under Settings → Services → Memes.

steps.title: Learn the classics on tap
prompt: What meme templates can you do? Show me a list, then make “this is fine” about my Monday meetings.

memes.outro: That's it — the shortest guide on this page, and easily the most popular one at parties.

travel.title: Your trip, planned end to end
travel.desc: Research, compare, decide — then carry a clean PDF itinerary and let it watch the prices.
travel.intro: By the end of this guide, planning a trip is a conversation: Wolffish researches flights, hotels, and neighborhoods, builds the day-by-day plan, and hands you a PDF itinerary to carry.

steps.title: Brief it like a travel agent
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send this — filled in with your trip:
prompt: Plan a 5-day trip to <city> in <month> for <who's going>, budget around <amount>. Compare flight options from <your city> and 3 well-located hotels, then suggest a day-by-day plan with food stops. Links for everything, please.

steps.title: Make it a carry-along PDF
prompt: Perfect — turn the final plan into a PDF itinerary: day-by-day schedule, addresses, times, and booking links.

steps.title: Let it watch fares while you decide
prompt: Check flights from <your city> to <city> every morning and message me only if a good round trip under <price> shows up.

travel.outro: You did the deciding; it did the tabs. Booking links, a pocket itinerary, and a fare-watcher running while you sleep.

price-watch.title: The patient deal hunter
price-watch.desc: It checks prices, stock, and slots while you live your life — and pings you exactly when it's time.
price-watch.intro: By the end of this guide, refreshing product pages is Wolffish's job: it checks on schedule and messages you only when the price drops or the item's back.

steps.title: Point it at the page
steps.body: In your Telegram bot chat, send this with a real product link:
prompt: Watch this page for me: <link>. Check it twice a day. Message me only when the price drops below <amount> or it's back in stock — otherwise stay quiet.

steps.title: Watch anything, the same way
steps.body: The same trick works on more than shopping:
prompt: Also watch <event tickets / a restock page / an appointment-booking page> daily and tell me the moment something opens up.
steps.note: Scheduled checks run on their own, without asking you first — so keep them read-only like these. Let it watch and report; do the buying yourself.

price-watch.outro: The deal now waits for you, not the other way around. When that message finally arrives, it feels like winning a tiny lottery.

meals.title: Dinner, decided
meals.desc: Weekly meal plans around your family's tastes — with the grocery list already written.
meals.intro: By the end of this guide, “what's for dinner?” is answered every Saturday: a week of meals that fit your household, plus one grocery list sorted by aisle.

steps.title: Introduce your household
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, tell it who it's cooking for — it remembers permanently:
prompt: Remember this: we're a family of <number>. <Dietary notes — e.g., halal only, one vegetarian, kids hate mushrooms.> Weekday dinners must take under 40 minutes.

steps.title: Order the weekly plan
prompt: Every Saturday at 10 am, send me a 7-dinner plan for the coming week based on what you know about us, plus one combined grocery list sorted by supermarket section.

steps.title: Use it on random Tuesdays too
prompt: I have chicken, rice, and a normal pantry. Three ideas for tonight, fastest first?

meals.outro: Rate the meals as you go — “less pasta”, “that stew was a hit” — and the plans quietly get better every week. That's the memory doing its job.

habits.title: A coach in your pocket
habits.desc: Daily check-ins, honest streaks, gentle accountability — for gym, reading, prayer, anything.
habits.intro: By the end of this guide, someone checks on you every evening — kindly, consistently, and with a memory. Habits survive on accountability, and now you have it built in.

steps.title: Declare the habits
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, send this with your real goals:
prompt: I'm building three habits: <habit 1>, <habit 2>, <habit 3>. Check in with me every evening at 9 pm — ask how each went, keep an honest log with streaks, and never guilt-trip me. On Sunday evenings send a weekly summary with one suggestion.

steps.title: Just answer honestly
steps.body: Each evening it asks; you reply in one line — “gym yes, reading no”. It logs, tracks streaks, and adjusts. Miss a day? It picks back up without drama.
steps.note: A voice note works too, on days when typing feels like a fourth habit.

habits.outro: Streaks, patterns, and a weekly mirror held up to your week — the boring secret behind every habit app, minus the app.

family.title: One assistant for the whole family
family.desc: Everyone texts the same helper: shared shopping list, family calendar, homework help, plans.
family.intro: By the end of this guide, your household has a shared brain: one Telegram bot every family member can message — it keeps the shopping list, fills the family calendar, and answers the kids' homework questions patiently.

steps.title: Let the family in
steps.body: Each family member sends /start to @userinfobot to get their ID number. Add all the IDs — comma-separated — to “Allowed user IDs” in Settings → Channels → Telegram, then share the bot's name with everyone.
steps.note: It answers one person at a time — if two people write at once, the second reply arrives a moment later.

steps.title: Give it the family job
steps.body: From your own chat with the bot, send:
prompt: You're our family assistant. Keep a shared shopping list anyone can add to or ask for. When someone mentions a family event, put it on the calendar and flag conflicts. Help the kids with homework by explaining patiently — never just giving answers. Be warm and brief.

steps.title: Watch it become the group memory
steps.body: “Add milk and batteries.” “What's on the list?” “When is Grandma's birthday dinner?” — anyone can ask, and everyone gets the same answers, because it's one assistant with one memory.

family.outro: The mental load of “who's tracking all this?” finally has an answer: the fish. One list, one calendar, one patient homework helper, shared by everyone.

vault.title: A memory for your paperwork
vault.desc: Send IDs, warranties, contracts, receipts as you get them — ask for anything months later.
vault.intro: By the end of this guide, “where did I put that document?” stops being a question. Photograph or forward paperwork the moment it appears; Wolffish files it, remembers it, and retrieves it on demand.

steps.title: Set the filing rule
steps.body: In your WhatsApp self-chat, send:
prompt: From now on, when I send you a document or a photo of paperwork, file it on my computer in a “Paperwork” folder organized by year and topic, give it a clear filename, and remember what it is and any expiry dates. Confirm in one line.

steps.title: Feed it your paper life
steps.body: Snap the insurance letter, forward the warranty PDF, photograph the receipt for the thing you might return. Each gets a one-line confirmation: filed, named, remembered.

steps.title: Ask like it's a person
prompt: Find my router warranty — when does it expire? Send me the file.
Zip everything in Paperwork from <last year> into one archive and send it to me for backup.

vault.outro: A filing cabinet that answers questions. The original files sit in normal folders on your computer — Wolffish is just the librarian who never forgets.

tidy.title: Clean your computer from your couch
tidy.desc: “Sort my Downloads.” “Free up space.” “Find that file from March.” — sent from your phone.
tidy.intro: By the end of this guide, the digital mess gets handled without you sitting at the desk: the Wolffish phone app becomes a remote control for cleaning, organizing, and finding things on your computer.

steps.title: Ask for a plan first
steps.body: From the phone app, send:
prompt: Look at my Downloads folder and propose a cleanup: what to keep, what to file into folders by type and year, what looks safe to delete. Show me the plan — don't touch anything yet.

steps.title: Approve, then let it work
prompt: Do it — but move things instead of deleting, and put anything you're unsure about in a “Review me” folder.
steps.note: Your computer needs to be on for the phone to reach it. Want it reachable always? See the “Always on” guide on this page.

steps.title: Use it as your finder
prompt: Find the PDF about <thing> I downloaded around <month> and send it to me here.

tidy.outro: The chore you've postponed for years is now a two-message conversation from the couch — plan, approve, done.

mcp.title: Plug in new superpowers
mcp.desc: MCP lets one paste connect Wolffish to thousands of tools — Notion, maps, databases, and more.
mcp.intro: MCP is a standard plug for AI tools: paste a server's address and Wolffish instantly learns its skills. This guide connects Notion as a worked example — the same three clicks work for thousands of other servers.

steps.title: Paste your first server
steps.body: In Wolffish, open Settings → MCP and paste this into “Command or URL”, then click Add and “Sign in” — your browser opens Notion's approval page:
steps.note: Only add servers you trust — a connected server's tools act on your behalf. Wolffish keeps each connection isolated and lets you test, disable, or remove it anytime.

steps.title: Use the new powers immediately
steps.body: In the app's chat (or any connected channel), try:
prompt: Create a Notion page called “Wolffish ideas” and add three things I could automate next based on what you know about me.

steps.title: Go exploring
steps.body: Any MCP server works the same way: paste a URL (remote) or a command (local), add an API key in the environment-variables box if the server needs one, done. Directories of servers are one search away — “MCP servers” — covering maps, music, smart homes, databases, and more.

mcp.outro: You've learned the universal plug. From here, Wolffish grows whenever you find a new server worth pasting — no waiting for anyone to build an integration.

cli.title: Wolffish in your terminal
cli.desc: For terminal fans: ask questions, pipe files in, script it — the same agent, no window.
cli.intro: The desktop app quietly installs a real command-line interface. Same brain, same memory, same conversations — reachable from any terminal, which is also what makes servers possible.

steps.title: Say hello from the terminal

cmd.code: wolffish "What's eating my disk space? Top 5 folders."

steps.note: If the command isn't found, open Settings → Channels → CLI in the app and click “Install command”, then open a new terminal.

cmd.code: cat confusing-bill.txt | wolffish -p "Anything unusual in this?"

steps.title: Drive the whole app from here
steps.body: Try “wolffish settings”, “wolffish automations”, or “wolffish conversations” — everything the app shows has a terminal view. Close the terminal and the agent keeps working.

cli.outro: You now have a personal agent one keystroke away in every terminal — and you've accidentally learned everything the “Always on” server guide needs.

vps.title: Always on: Wolffish in the cloud
vps.desc: Put it on a $5/month server and it never sleeps — laptop closed, automations still running.
vps.intro: Everything on this page runs while your computer is awake. This guide removes that condition: Wolffish moves to a small rented server that's on 24/7 — briefings on time, watchers watching, phone always connected. This is the power-user setup, but every command is given below.

steps.title: Rent a small server
steps.body: Any provider works — Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, Lightsail. Choose Ubuntu 24.04 and the smallest size (~$5/month). You'll get an IP address and a root login; connect from your terminal:

steps.title: Install Wolffish on it
steps.body: One line — same installer as the desktop:

steps.title: Give it its brain
steps.body: Create a DeepSeek key at platform.deepseek.com (sign up → add a few dollars → “API Keys” → create), then on the server:

cmd.note: paste the key when asked — it's hidden and tested

steps.title: Connect Telegram
steps.body: Create a bot with @BotFather (send /newbot, copy the token) and get your ID from @userinfobot — then:

steps.title: Pair your phone to the server
steps.body: Install the Wolffish phone app, then generate a pairing code on the server and type it into the app under “Connect to Desktop”:
steps.note: The server exposes nothing to the internet — no ports, no web panel. Your phone and Telegram reach it through outbound, end-to-end encrypted connections only.

vps.outro: Your agent now lives in the cloud, awake around the clock: morning briefings on the dot, watchers that never blink, and your phone connected from anywhere on earth. Set up any other guide on this page — it now runs 24/7.
